title: Optogenetic Stimulation of Enteric Neurons in Murine Large Intestine
author: Dante Heredia
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgr9jv96

steps.title: Excise the colon
steps.instruction: Perform dissection and experiments in the dark under infrared illumination.

substeps.instruction: Carefully excise the whole colon into a Sylguard lined dissection dish containing oxygenated Krebs-ringer solution.

steps.title: Mount the colon on capillary tube
steps.instruction: Position the colon over a fire-polished capillary tube (1.5-mm diameter) that is longer than the colon.

substeps.instruction: Mount an artificial pellet to the capillary glass.
Position the colon so the pellet is in the middle.
Fix the capillary glass to the bottom of the organ bath using the ends protruding from each colonic opening.

steps.title: Attach force transducers
steps.instruction: Connect three force transducers (model TST125C; Biopac Systems, Santa Barbara, CA) to the proximal, transverse, and distal segments of the colon using suture silk.

steps.title: Set resting tension
steps.instruction: Set the initial resting tension to 8 mN.

substeps.instruction: Monitor tension using an MP100 interface.
Record data on a PC running Acqknowledge software 3.2.6 (Biopac Systems).

steps.title: Perform optogenetic stimulation
steps.instruction: Once spontaneous colonic migrating motor complexes (CMMCs) are detected, apply blue light stimulation.

substeps.instruction: Option 1: Shine blue light continuously for 20s using a hand-held laser (450 nm Sapphire Galaxy 3; ZBolt; Happy Valley, OR) mounted on a clamp stand 30 cm above the preparation.
Option 2: Use 4 pairs of LEDs placed on either side of the colon, connected to a wire driven by an SD9 stimulator at 5Hz (20ms pulsewidth) for 5, 20, or 60 seconds.

steps.title: Administer drugs and re-stimulate
steps.instruction: Perform several control light stimulations, then perfuse drugs and repeat the light stimulations.
